prompt:
You are the prosecutor. Your job is to FALSIFY the claims below. For each claim, either:
(a) state a concrete scenario in which it is false, AND propose a minimal test or command
    that would demonstrate it; or (b) state you could not falsify it.
You may also raise NEW hypotheses about behaviour the change silently alters.
Every hypothesis must cite exact diff lines. No confidence numbers.
inputs: git history: commit 1a74a620, v3.1.0..v3.1.1 TypeCollector.cs diff
note: Hypotheses only. A hypothesis counts as a finding only after the evidence engine runs its test_sketch and it reproduces. Nothing here was executed.

attacks.scenario: The three tests already pass on the base commit, because the regression introduced in v3.1.1 is not in the base. Then the tests are evidence of behaviour, not of a fix.
attacks.test_sketch: Copy SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs into a base worktree and run: dotnet test tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests -f net8.0 --filter FullyQualifiedName~SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests. Expected if the claim needs the fix: 3 failures. Expected if the regression is absent: all pass.
attacks.holds_if: MemberWithoutKey, AllowPrivateRequired, MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObject fail on base

attacks.scenario: Duplicate keys already produce MsgPack005 without a crash on base for suppressed types, so the new guards change nothing observable there.
attacks.test_sketch: Same run as P-2234-1 for DuplicateIntKeys, DuplicateStringKeys, MixedKeyKinds; then revert only the two ContainsKey guards on head and rerun; record which tests go red.
attacks.holds_if: tests go red when the guards are reverted
attacks.falsified_if: tests stay green with the guards reverted

attacks.scenario: A valid contract whose members are all attributed with unique, same-kind keys is untouched by the hunk; a contract with a skipped member differs only in invalid code. Attack: a type with int keys and a member whose key attribute carries a null string value reaches the skip path although the code is not obviously invalid.
attacks.test_sketch: Generator run on [MessagePackObject] class with [Key(0)] int A and [Key((string)null)] int B; compare formatter output base vs head.
attacks.falsified_if: output differs for a contract with no analyzer error

cited_lines.quote: continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.

attacks.scenario: The cause of the regression is the placement of the suppression early return (top of the method in v3.1.1+, end of the method here). The diff does not move it. Run the tests on a v3.1.1 worktree (which has the regression) without the diff: expected red; then with the diff applied: if still red, the diff does not fix #2234.
attacks.test_sketch: git worktree add ../wt-311 v3.1.1 (no commit); copy the 3 tests; run; then git diff base..head | git apply in that worktree; run again.
attacks.holds_if: red on v3.1.1 without the diff and green with it

attacks.scenario: The runtime test asserts behaviour that no hunk in the diff modifies; it should pass on base and on head.
attacks.test_sketch: dotnet test tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.ExecutionTests -f net8.0 --filter FullyQualifiedName~SuppressedSourceGenerationTests on both worktrees.

attacks.scenario: Generator-only build with the analyzer disabled: a mixed-key type loses a member from the formatter and nothing is reported.
attacks.test_sketch: CSharpGeneratorDriver run (no analyzer) on [MessagePackObject] class M { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} [Key("b")] public int B {get;set;} }; read the generated formatter and check that B is absent; check runResult.Diagnostics is empty.
attacks.holds_if: B is serialized or an error is produced

cited_lines.quote: continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.

attacks.scenario: A suppressed type with a member attributed by a type derived from KeyAttribute reaches the MsgPack016 condition; the README says 016 is not reported but the condition cited keeps MemberNeedsKey for suppressed types with a derived key.
attacks.test_sketch: Analyzer test: [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] class with [DerivedKey(0)] member; expect no MsgPack016 per README.

attacks.test_sketch: Analyzer test: private nested class marked [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]; expect {|MsgPack012:...|}.

cited_lines.quote: Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

new_hypotheses.text: The base commit predates the regression: the eight analyzer tests pass on base, so Time Machine will show pass-to-pass for the tests that claim to evidence #2234.

Duplicate keys crashed the analyzer for every type, not only suppressed ones, because the Add calls were unconditional; the real #2234 symptom on master may be a different failure from the one these guards remove.
new_hypotheses.test_sketch: Run DuplicateKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailureForGeneratedTypes on base: if it passes, the guards were not needed for non-suppressed types.
